sections.t: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

Chapter I.-The Doctrine of the Resurrection of the Body Brought to Light by the Gospel. The Faintest Glimpses of Something Like It Occasionally Met with in Heathenism. Inconsistencies of Pagan Teaching.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter II.-The Jewish Sadducees a Link Between the Pagan Philosophers and the Heretics on This Doctrine. Its Fundamental Importance Asserted. The Soul Fares Better Than the Body, in Heretical Estimation, as to Its Future State. Its Extinction, However, Was Held by One Lucan.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter III.-Some Truths Held Even by the Heathen, They Were, However, More Often Wrong Both in Religious Opinions and in Moral Practice. The Heathen Not to Be Followed in Their Ignorance of the Christian Mystery. The Heretics Perversely Prone to Follow Them.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter IV.-Heathens and Heretics Alike in Their Vilification of the Flesh and Its Functions, the Ordinary Cavils Against the Final Restitution of So Weak and Ignoble a Substance.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter V.-Some Considerations in Reply Eulogistic of the Flesh. It Was Created by God. The Body of Man Was, in Fact, Previous to His Soul.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter VI.-Not the Lowliness of the Material, But the Dignity and Skill of the Maker, Must Be Remembered, in Gauging the Excellence of the Flesh. Christ Partook of Our Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter VII.-The Earthy Material of Which Flesh is Created Wonderfully Improved by God's Manipulation. By the Addition of the Soul in Man's Constitution It Became the Chief Work in the Creation.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter VIII.-Christianity, by Its Provision for the Flesh, Has Put on It the Greatest Honour. The Privileges of Our Religion in Closest Connection with Our Flesh. Which Also Bears a Large Share in the Duties and Sacrifices of Religion.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter IX.-God's Love for the Flesh of Man, as Developed in the Grace of Christ Towards It. The Flesh the Best Means of Displaying the Bounty and Power of God.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter X.-Holy Scripture Magnifies the Flesh, as to Its Nature and Its Prospects.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XI.-The Power of God Fully Competent to Effect the Resurrection of the Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XII.-Some Analogies in Nature Which Corroborate the Resurrection of the Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XIII.-From Our Author's View of a Verse in the Ninety-Second Psalm, the Phoenix is Made a Symbol of the Resurrection of Our Bodies.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XIV.-A Sufficient Cause for the Resurrection of the Flesh Occurs in the Future Judgment of Man, It Will Take Cognisance of the Works of the Body No Less Than of the Soul.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XV.-As the Flesh is a Partaker with the Soul in All Human Conduct, So Will It Be in the Recompense of Eternity.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XVI.-The Heretics Called the Flesh "The Vessel of the Soul," In Order to Destroy the Responsibility of the Body. Their Cavil Turns Upon Themselves and Shows the Flesh to Be a Sharer in Human Actions.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XVII.-The Flesh Will Be Associated with the Soul in Enduring the Penal Sentences of the Final Judgment.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XVIII.-Scripture Phrases and Passages Clearly Assert "The Resurrection of the Dead." The Force of This Very Phrase Explained as Indicating the Prominent Place of the Flesh in the General Resurrection.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XIX.-The Sophistical Sense Put by Heretics on the Phrase "Resurrection of the Dead," As If It Meant the Moral Change of a New Life.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XX.-Figurative Senses Have Their Foundation in Literal Fact. Besides, the Allegorical Style is by No Means the Only One Found in the Prophetic Scriptures, as Alleged by the Heretics.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXI.-No Mere Metaphor in the Phrase Resurrection of the Dead. In Proportion to the Importance of Eternal Truths, is the Clearness of Their Scriptural Enunciation.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXII.-The Scripture Bid Our Supposing Either that the Resurrection is Already Past, or that It Takes Place Immediately at Death. Our Hopes and Prayers Point to the Last Great Day as the Period of Its Accomplishment.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXIII.-Sundry Passages of St. Paul, Which Speak of a Spiritual Resurrection, Compatible with the Future Resurrection of the Body, Which is Even Assumed in Them.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXIV.-Other Passages Quoted from St. Paul, Which Categorically Assert the Resurrection of the Flesh at the Final Judgment.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXV.-St. John, in the Apocalypse, Equally Explicit in Asserting the Same Great Doctrine.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXVI.-Even the Metaphorical Descriptions of This Subject in the Scriptures Point to the Bodily Resurrection, the Only Sense Which Secures Their Consistency and Dignity.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXVII.-Certain Metaphorical Terms Explained of the Resurrection of the Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXVIII.-Prophetic Things and Actions, as Well as Words, Attest This Great Doctrine.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXIX.-Ezekiel's Vision of the Dry Bones Quoted.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXX.-This Vision Interpreted by Tertullian of the Resurrection of the Bodies of the Dead. A Chronological Error of Our Author, Who Supposes that Ezekiel in His Ch. XXXI. Prophesied Before the Captivity.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXI.-Other Passages Out of the Prophets Applied to the Resurrection of the Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXII.-Even Unburied Bodies Will Be Raised Again. Whatever Befalls Them God Will Restore Them Again. Jonah's Case Quoted in Illustration of God's Power.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXIII.-So Much for the Prophetic Scriptures. In the Gospels, Christ's Parables, as Explained by Himself, Have a Clear Reference to the Resurrection of the Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXIV.-Christ Plainly Testifies to the Resurrection of the Entire Man. Not in His Soul Only, Without the Body.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXV.-Explanation of What is Meant by the Body, Which is to Be Raised Again. Not the Corporeality of the Soul.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXVI.-Christ's Refutation of the Sadducees, and Affirmation of Catholic Doctrine.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXVII.-Christ's Assertion About the Unprofitableness of the Flesh Explained Consistently with Our Doctrine.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXVIII.-Christ, by Raising the Dead, Attested in a Practical Way the Doctrine of the Resurrection of the Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XXXIX.-Additional Evidence Afforded to Us in the Acts of the Apostles.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XL.-Sundry Passages of St. Paul Which Attest Our Doctrine Rescued from the Perversions of Heresy.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLI.-The Dissolution of Our Tabernacle Consistent with the Resurrection of Our Bodies.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLII.-Death Changes, Without Destroying, Our Mortal Bodies. Remains of the Giants.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLIII.-No Disparagement of Our Doctrine in St. Paul's Phrase, Which Calls Our Residence in the Flesh Absence from the Lord.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLIV.-Sundry Other Passages of St. Paul Explained in a Sentence Confirmatory of Our Doctrine.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLV.-The Old Man and the New Man of St. Paul Explained.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLVI.-It is the Works of the Flesh, Not the Substance of the Flesh, Which St. Paul Always Condemns.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLVII.-St. Paul, All Through, Promises Eternal Life to the Body.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLVIII.-Sundry Passages in the Great Chapter of the Resurrection of the Dead Explained in Defence of Our Doctrine.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter XLIX.-The Same Subject Continued. What Does the Apostle Exclude from the Dead? Certainly Not the Substance of the Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter L.-In What Sense Flesh and Blood are Excluded from the Kingdom of God.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LI.-The Session of Jesus in His Incarnate Nature at the Right Hand of God a Guarantee of the Resurrection of Our Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LII.-From St. Paul's Analogy of the Seed We Learn that the Body Which Died Will Rise Again, Garnished with the Appliances of Eternal Life.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LIII.-Not the Soul, But the Natural Body Which Died, is that Which is to Rise Again. The Resurrection of Lazarus Commented on. Christ's Resurrection, as the Second Adam, Guarantees Our Own.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LIV.-Death Swallowed Up of Life. Meaning of This Phrase in Relation to the Resurrection of the Body.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LV.-The Change of a Thing's Condition is Not the Destruction of Its Substance. The Application of This Principle to Our Subject.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LVI.-The Procedure of the Last Judgment, and Its Awards, Only Possible on the Identity of the Risen Body with Our Present Flesh.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LVII.-Our Bodies, However Mutilated Before or After Death, Shall Recover Their Perfect Integrity in the Resurrection. Illustration of the Enfranchised Slave.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LVIII.-From This Perfection of Our Restored Bodies Will Flow the Consciousness of Undisturbed Joy and Peace.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LIX.-Our Flesh in the Resurrection Capable, Without Losing Its Essential Identity, of Bearing the Changed Conditions of Eternal Life, or of Death Eternal.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LX.-All the Characteristics of Our Bodies-Sex, Various Limbs, Etc.-Will Be Retained, Whatever Change of Functions These May Have, of Which Point, However, We are No Judges. Analogy of the Repaired Ship.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LXI.-The Details of Our Bodily Sex, and of the Functions of Our Various Members. Apology for the Necessity Which Heresy Imposes of Hunting Up All Its Unblushing Cavils.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LXII.-Our Destined Likeness to the Angels in the Glorious Life of the Resurrection.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh

sections.t: Chapter LXIII.-Conclusion. The Resurrection of the Flesh in Its Absolute Identity and Perfection. Belief of This Had Become Weak. Hopes for Its Refreshing Restoration Under the Influences of the Paraclete.
path: On the Resurrection of the Flesh
